items.name: Fresh lotus seed
items.prabhava: The pond-fresh seed of the sacred lotus — cooling and gently binding; eaten raw from the pod in season, it shares makhana's calming, pitta-friendly nature.
combinations: eaten raw from the fresh pod (seasonal treat)
in kheer when slightly mature
lightly sautéed with ghee and rock salt
items.preparation: Tender green seeds shelled from fresh lotus pods, the bitter germ removed, eaten raw or lightly cooked. A brief-season delicacy of the water gardens.

items.name: Baby turnip with greens
combinations: root and greens cooked together (Kashmiri gogji style)
with mustard oil and dry chilies
in winter meat stews (regional)
contraindications: thyroid caution with heavy raw brassica intake
items.preparation: Young winter turnips cooked whole with their peppery greens — the root sweetens as the greens bite. Cook through; raw turnip is harder on both gut and gland.

items.name: Sweet parwal variant
items.prabhava: Patola holds a rare classical rank — tridoshic, pathya (wholesome for the sick), the convalescent's vegetable; the sweet strain is its gentlest expression.
combinations: simple ghee-jeera sabzi for the recovering
parwal-potato curry (everyday)
stuffed parwal for festive tables
contraindications: none significant — a classical pathya vegetable
items.preparation: Tender sweet pointed gourds cooked simply — ghee, cumin, a little turmeric. When the texts want one vegetable for a patient, patola is the habitual answer.

items.name: Split red lentil
items.prabhava: Grahi — masura gently binds the gut; the classical dal for loose digestion, and the fastest-cooking of the everyday pulses.
combinations: ghee-jeera-hing tadka (the vata counterweight)
with rice as everyday dal-chawal
lemon at serving brightens without souring
items.preparation: Quick-cooking split lentil, simmered soft and tempered. Being grahi, it suits loose guts and monsoon bellies better than hard-dry constitutions.

items.name: White chickpea
combinations: chole with ajwain, ginger and anardana (the digestion-wise masala)
soaked overnight, always
with bhatura (festival) or rice (weekday)
contraindications: vata excess / gas and bloating (the classic offender)
items.preparation: Soak overnight, cook thoroughly, spice assertively — chana's cooling dryness provokes vata unless ginger, ajwain and fat intervene. Midday food.

usda.name: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, raw

items.name: Black chickpea
items.prabhava: The desi chana — denser, more fibrous and more mineral-rich than its white cousin; the traditional strength food of wrestlers, soaked and eaten at dawn.
combinations: soaked overnight with ginger and salt (akhara breakfast)
ghugni-style curry (east India)
sundal with coconut (south, festival)
items.preparation: Longer soaking and cooking than kabuli; sprouting or overnight soaking is traditional. Robust nutrition that demands robust agni — earn it with exercise, as the wrestlers do.

usda.name: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, raw

items.name: Split black gram
items.prabhava: Balya and vrishya — masha is the classical strength-and-virility pulse, the anti-mung: heavy, warming, building; medicine for the depleted, burden for the sedentary.
combinations: dal makhani-style slow cooking with ghee
with hing and ginger (mandatory carminatives)
in idli-dosa batter (fermentation lightens it)
items.preparation: Slow-cooked soft with warming carminatives; fermentation (idli, dosa, vada) is tradition's way of taming its heaviness. Winter food for active bodies.

items.name: Whole black gram
items.prabhava: Masha entire, skin on — heavier still than the split dal; the substance of dal makhani and the classical vajikarana (virility) diet.
combinations: overnight-simmered with ginger, garlic and ghee (makhani tradition)
with rajma in mixed winter dals
a long walk afterwards (the missing ingredient)
items.preparation: The whole bean needs the longest soak and slowest simmer of any dal. Reserve for cold-season middays and appetites backed by labor.

items.name: Garlic (fresh bulb)
items.prabhava: Rasona — 'lacking one taste' (sour) yet holding five; classical rasayana for vata, heart and joints, potent enough that the texts fence it with cautions and the sattvic kitchens exclude it.
combinations: cooked in ghee or milk (classical rasona ksheerapaka for vata)
with warming winter dals and meats
crushed and rested before cooking (folk-modern practice)
contraindications: pitta excess — acidity, bleeding tendencies, skin heat
items.preparation: Fresh cloves cooked into food or simmered in milk for the classical vata preparation. Raw garlic is strongest and harshest; cooking rounds its edges.

items.name: Black-eyed pea
combinations: curried with tomato-onion masala
sundal-style with coconut
with garlic tadka (gas insurance)
items.preparation: Among the friendlier beans — quicker to cook and gentler than chana. Soak briefly, cook soft, temper with garlic or hing as habit.

usda.name: Cowpeas, common (blackeyes, crowder, southern), mature seeds, raw

items.name: Moth bean
items.prabhava: The desert legume — makushtha thrives where nothing else grows; Maharashtra sprouts it into misal's usal base, Rajasthan fries it into bhujia.
combinations: sprouted into usal (Maharashtrian)
matki chi bhaji with goda masala
with kokum for the sour note
contraindications: vata excess / gas-prone (sprout or spice well)
weak agni in fried bhujia form
items.preparation: Small drought-hardy beans, best sprouted — sprouting shortens cooking and softens the legume's windiness. Usal-misal is its natural habitat.

items.name: Horse gram
items.prabhava: Ashmarighna — the stone-breaker: kulattha is the classical prescription for urinary calculi, and the hot-sharp legume that scrapes kapha and fat from the channels.
combinations: kollu rasam / soup for cold-season kapha
gahat dal in the Himalayan winter (Uttarakhand)
decoction water taken for urinary gravel (traditional)
viruddha: with milk at the same meal (traditional caution)
items.preparation: Soaked and simmered into soups, rasams and dals; even its cooking water is kept as medicine. Winter and monsoon food — hot, dry constitutions should pass.

items.name: Dry field peas
combinations: ghugni with ginger and cumin (Bengal/Odisha)
in undhiyu and mixed winter curries
generous hing in the tempering (essential)
contraindications: vata excess — the windiest of the common pulses
items.preparation: Long soak, thorough cooking, assertive hing-ginger spicing. Classical texts rank the pea family high for taste and higher for flatulence — respect the tempering.

usda.name: Peas, green, split, mature seeds, raw

items.name: Hyacinth bean
combinations: Gujarati valnu shaak with jaggery and kokum
dalimbi usal (Maharashtrian, sprouted)
ajwain-garlic tempering as standard
contraindications: pitta with burning digestion (classical vidahi note)
items.reviewNote: Classical nishpava is described as vidahi (burning) and vata-provoking; regional cuisines counter with jaggery-kokum. Facets follow the classical caution.
items.preparation: Soaked, often sprouted and skinned (dalimbi), always well cooked with sour-sweet balancing. A strong-flavoured bean that repays careful preparation.

items.name: Fresh green pea
combinations: matar paneer (the winter classic)
in pulao and poha
with ginger and cumin in ghee (the vata answer)
contraindications: vata excess / gas-prone (milder than dry peas, still a pea)
raw in quantity for weak digestion
items.preparation: Sweet winter peas cooked fresh — far lighter than their dried form. Ghee, cumin and ginger remain the wise defaults for any pea.

items.name: Brown lentil
combinations: whole masoor dal with garlic tadka
sprouted into salads (lightly steamed)
with rice or roti as everyday protein
contraindications: constipation-prone vata (grahi tendency, milder than split)
items.preparation: Whole masoor with skin — earthier and slower-cooking than the split dal, slightly less grahi. Soak an hour, cook soft, temper as usual.

items.name: Fava bean
combinations: young pods cooked whole as sabzi
mature beans in mixed dals
with dill or ajwain (regional carminative pairing)
contraindications: G6PD deficiency — favism risk, strictly avoid
items.preparation: Young pods cook like flat beans; mature seeds need soaking, skinning and thorough boiling. The G6PD (favism) caution is absolute where ancestry suggests risk.

items.name: Sprouted mung
items.prabhava: The best pulse, sprouted — mudga is already the texts' favourite legume; sprouting enlivens it further, though classical opinion asks that sprouts be cooked, not raw.
combinations: lightly steamed with lemon and rock salt
misal-usal style with light spicing
in warm salads — steamed beats raw for vata
contraindications: raw sprouts in quantity for vata and weak agni (classical virudhahara-adjacent caution)
items.preparation: Mung soaked and sprouted 1–2 days, then lightly steamed or sautéed. Raw sprout salads are a modern habit; the gut prefers them warmed.

usda.name: Mung beans, mature seeds, sprouted, raw

items.name: Sprouted black chickpea
combinations: steamed with onion, lemon and green chili (chaat style)
the wrestler's dawn handful with ginger
lightly sautéed sundal
contraindications: vata excess / gas-prone (lighter than unsprouted, still chana)
weak agni (steam rather than eat raw)
items.preparation: Kala chana soaked a day, sprouted a day, then steamed or sautéed. Sprouting redeems some of chana's heaviness — the traditional strength breakfast, made kinder.

items.name: Roasted gram flour (sattu)
items.prabhava: The classical saktu — pre-roasted, pre-digested traveler's flour that needs no fire: stirred into water it cools, satiates and steadies; Bihar's summer against the loo wind.
combinations: sattu sharbat with lemon, salt or jaggery (the summer drink)
kneaded into litti stuffing
classical rule: never at night, never twice a day, never with heavy meals
viruddha: classical saktu cautions: not at night, not after meals, not with milk in excess
contraindications: weak agni with heavy sattu preparations
items.preparation: Chana (with or without barley) roasted and milled; stirred into cool water as drink or dough. The texts prescribe exactly how saktu is taken — its rules are part of the food.

items.name: Roasted chana (bhuna)
combinations: with jaggery (the classic gud-chana pair — balances the dryness)
handful with tea as evening snack
ground into instant chutney bases
contraindications: vata excess / dry constitutions (pair with jaggery or ghee)
dental caution with very hard-roasted grams
items.preparation: Sand- or fire-roasted whole gram, skin rubbed off — the frugal protein snack of the subcontinent. Jaggery alongside is not indulgence, it is formulation.

items.name: Peanut (raw)
combinations: soaked overnight (softens and lightens)
boiled in salted water (coastal style — gentler than roasted)
in sabudana khichdi and poha as crush
contraindications: aflatoxin caution — only fresh, well-stored nuts
items.preparation: Raw peanuts digest hardest — soaking or boiling is the traditional mercy. An oil-rich legume masquerading as a nut; treat it as a heavy food.

items.name: Peanut (roasted)
combinations: winter street handful with jaggery
crushed over poha and upma
in chikki (see peanut chikki)
items.preparation: Dry-roasting lightens the raw nut a step and adds warmth. The winter fire-side snack — a handful, not a packet.

items.name: Lima bean
combinations: pavta bhaji with goda masala (Maharashtrian)
double-bean curry (South)
with garlic and ajwain as always
contraindications: undercooked beans (cyanogenic glycosides — always boil well, water discarded)
items.preparation: Buttery when well cooked, risky when not — lima beans must be boiled thoroughly with the first water discarded. Then they are the softest of the big beans.

usda.name: Lima beans, large, mature seeds, raw

items.name: White peas (safed vatana)
combinations: ragda under pattice (Mumbai street classic)
ghugni with ginger and green chili
tamarind-jaggery finish (cuts the windiness pleasantly)
contraindications: vata excess — among the gassiest pulses
items.preparation: Overnight soak and pressure-cook to collapse; ginger, hing and sour-sweet finishing are structural, not optional. Street tradition serves it heavy — home wisdom serves it at midday.
